checks.label: Squaring both sides of an equation may introduce extra solutions not valid for the original equation: I = √ of a number, squared, lets in its negative root as well, which fails when put back

Boyle's law: the absolute pressure and volume of a given mass of confined gas are inversely proportional, provided the temperature remains unchanged, so p₁V₁ = p₂V₂ on every Boyle's law screen, with absolute pressures, and more pressure goes with less volume
Standard atmosphere: 101 325 Pa, about 1 bar (100 000 Pa), so with that exact figure the gauge screen's 2 bar and 5 bar readings still give about 5 L
Voltage drop per ampere per metre: mV/A/m × amps × metres gives millivolts, and a thousand millivolts make a volt, on every voltage-drop screen

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and every wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives, its check failing: a square halved or left on; the root taken before the ÷ R; both roots kept; a step done again instead of undone; a × undone by taking away; a division the wrong way round; gauge readings put in as absolute; the × 1000 left out; the steps on L done again; I² read as 2I or left as I

Every card screen, finished, puts each amount under its letter in that letter's unit, draws the steps done to the letter wanted, naming what they end on, and, under them, their undo, last step first, then the rearranged formula (with its units check for Boyle's law and the voltage-drop rule) and the check; each slip's check (and wrong formula) is in the warning colour; nothing leaves the picture

Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the answer: the letter wanted is a '?', no undo box is lit or filled, no rearranged formula or check, and the gauge screen shows no absolute pressure

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart
